Asif, class eleven. Our school has a trip every term, and for three years I have packed the same way: from a list. It's on a card in my drawer: ID card, water bottle, charger, two pens, raincoat, sun hat, snacks.
The night before a trip I lay everything on the bed, tick it off, then zip the bag. It takes ten minutes, and I don't have to think. My sister Zainab laughs at the card, but last term she forgot her ID card and had to phone home from the gate.
A list works because the job is always the same. For something new I'd need more than a card.

qa.q: What is on the card in Asif's drawer?
qa.a: The card lists an ID card, water bottle, charger, two pens, raincoat, sun hat and snacks.

qa.q: How does Asif feel about packing from the list?
qa.a: Asif feels comfortable and untroubled, since it takes ten minutes and there is no need to think.

qa.q: What could Asif do if the trip were a new kind, such as a camp?
qa.a: Asif could ask the teacher what to bring and write a new list, since the old card fits only the same repeated job.

qa.q: How might Zainab feel about laughing at the card, then forgetting the ID?
qa.a: Zainab may feel a bit embarrassed at having to phone home from the gate, and may see the card as more useful than she thought.

grounding: A student who packs for similar school trips uses a fixed list because a repeated task with known steps is faster than fresh thinking.

Class teacher's note: Class 9 hill trip, packing morning

This is our third school trip this year, and Naveen's packing always takes him ten minutes while others take an hour. This morning I asked him how. He pulled out a laminated card from his bag. "It's my trip list," he said. "Same trips every term, same things: jacket, torch, water bottle, two pairs of socks, medicines Mummy packs, ID card. I don't want to think about it every time. I just tick." Lalremsiami, standing next to him, asked if she could copy it. Naveen said, "Change it for you, though. You need your inhaler." I have asked Naveen to share his list with the class for the next trip.

qa.q: What was on Naveen's trip list?
qa.a: Jacket, torch, water bottle, two pairs of socks, medicines Mummy packs and ID card.

qa.q: Why does Naveen like using the same list?
qa.a: He feels relaxed and efficient not having to think afresh, since the trips and things needed are the same each term.

qa.q: What else could Naveen add to make the list better?
qa.a: A line for anything special to a particular trip, like rain gear, so the routine stays fast but flexible.

qa.q: How might Lalremsiami see Naveen's advice to change the list for her?
qa.a: She might feel cared for and see that a checklist works best when it fits the person using it.

grounding: A student packing for repeated school trips uses a fixed list, since a routine is faster than fresh thinking for a known task.

Friday

Packed for the science camp in eight minutes. Record! Siddharth came over and watched me with his mouth open. He'd been packing since last night and still forgot his torch. Here's my trick: after the first trip in Class 8, I wrote a list on a card. Toothbrush, towel, torch, rain jacket, water bottle, notebook, two pens, charger. We go on the same kind of trip every term, so why think it up again every time? I just read the card and tick. My brain doesn't have to do anything. Last time I forgot socks, so I added socks. Siddharth wants to make his own card now. I'm Deepak, and I'm officially the packing champion of our class.

qa.q: How long did Deepak take to pack?
How does Deepak feel about the packing list?
qa.a: Deepak feels proud and pleased, calling it a record and joking about being the packing champion.

qa.q: When would a fixed list not be enough?
qa.a: For a new kind of trip, like one to the snow, Deepak would need to think afresh about what's different.

qa.q: How might Siddharth feel watching Deepak pack?
qa.a: Siddharth seems amazed and a bit envious after packing since last night and still forgetting his torch.

grounding: A student who packs for similar trips each term uses a fixed list, since a routine is faster than fresh thinking.
